name: Pyroelectric Sebum Volatilization Projector
description:
The PSVP-1 uses a focused pyroelectric excitation beam to rapidly heat the lipid-rich sebaceous secretions present on human skin to their volatilization threshold, producing a thin layer of ignitable vapor directly against the target's epidermis. A secondary piezoelectric ignition pulse, delivered 0.4 seconds after the primary beam, ignites this vapor layer. The result is a flash-burn effect that originates on the skin's surface rather than being applied externally — it cannot be blocked by standard fire-resistant outerwear because the fuel source is the body itself.

The weapon's tactical novelty is its ability to defeat fire-protective equipment that would otherwise render incendiary weapons ineffective. Flame-retardant suits, ceramic composite armor, and even experimental aerogel body armor provide no meaningful protection against an ignition event that begins at the skin layer. The burn produced is typically superficial to partial-thickness depending on exposure duration, but the psychological effect of fire appearing beneath armor is profound and immediately disabling in most subjects.

The PSVP-1 is a Ringo Corponation product, developed under a contract that has never been publicly disclosed and which Ringo's legal division actively suppresses inquiry into. The weapon saw limited deployment in a corporate territorial dispute in the outer sectors approximately three years ago, after which two municipal investigators who were building a war crimes case died in unrelated accidents. The weapon's existence is known primarily through survivor accounts and a single partially intact unit recovered by an independent forensic team.
specifications:
effective range: 2–12 meters
power source: Dual-cell pyroelectric and piezoelectric capacitor array, 11 discharge cycles
primary beam duration: 0.4 seconds per cycle
ignition delay: 0.4 seconds post-primary beam
burn depth: Superficial to partial-thickness (exposure-dependent)
weight: 2.2 kg
form factor: Compact pistol configuration with dual emitter ports
armor penetration: Effective against all fire-resistant and most composite body armor
tactical_use: The PSVP-1 is used primarily to defeat armored targets in close-quarters engagements where conventional weapons have been neutralized by protective equipment. Operators typically fire once to establish the volatilization effect, then the ignition fires automatically. A single discharge is usually sufficient for incapacitation due to pain response even when burn depth is limited. The weapon is rarely used for lethality — it is a compliance and deterrence tool among those who possess it, as the psychological effect of knowing one's armor is irrelevant is significant. Its short range limits utility in open engagements.
cultural_context: The PSVP-1 exists in GLMZ's criminal and shadow-military ecosystem as a kind of horror story. Most people who know about it know someone who knows someone — it sits at the edge of verified reality. Among armored security professionals, it represents an existential anxiety: the idea that the protection they rely on could be made worse than useless. Ringo Corponation's involvement is widely suspected in underground circles but unprovable, and those who have tried to prove it have encountered consistent obstruction. The weapon has no street name that is used casually — it is spoken of carefully.
known_users: A small number of black-market weapons brokers who treat it as a prestige commodity
At least one outer-sector gang that acquired a unit and has used it for territorial enforcement
story_hooks: A burn victim in a hospital shows an injury pattern that a trauma surgeon quietly identifies as inconsistent with any known incendiary — the surgeon contacts someone they trust rather than filing a report.
A partially functional PSVP-1 surfaces at a black-market auction; multiple parties with very different agendas want it, and the auction is about to go violently wrong.
Someone inside Ringo Corponation is willing to hand over the original development contract documentation in exchange for extraction from the company's residential campus.

The outer-sector gang using the recovered unit has begun making demands on neighboring territories, and everyone knows they have something that changes the equation — but nobody wants to be first to find out exactly what.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, deliberately clinical pistol with a distinctly medical aesthetic corrupted by weapons engineering. Twin barrel ports dominate the muzzle, asymmetrically offset. The overall silhouette is squat and forward-heavy, resembling a dermatological device more than a firearm—which is precisely intentional obfuscation. The grip tapers slightly, designed for precision trigger work rather than sustained fire.
physical_description.dimensions: 18 cm length, 6 cm grip width, 4 cm height at slide. Dual emitter ports protrude 2.5 cm from muzzle face.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 2.2 kg—users often misjudge its heft initially. The weight distribution favors the muzzle due to capacitor array clustering, creating a subtle downward bias that aids aim stability but feels slightly unnatural in untrained hands.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite chassis with embedded pyroelectric and piezoelectric ceramic matrices. Interior architecture visible through semi-translucent sidewall panels—a signature design choice suggesting confidence in the technology's stability, or deliberate intimidation.
physical_description.finish: Matte forensic white with gunmetal-gray piezo coupling rings around each emitter port. The polymer shows a faint opalescent sheen under certain angles—a byproduct of the embedded ceramic layering rather than aesthetic coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominating clinical white, interrupted by three gunmetal accent bands (trigger guard, charging mechanism, capacitor release lever). Safety indicator is a subdued bio-indicator orange dot on the slide.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer with deliberate finger-well geometry. The texture is slightly tacky, engineered for sweat resistance during high-stress scenarios. The grip has an almost medical grip-tape feel—clinical, precise, divorced from traditional weapon ergonomics.
distinctive_features: Dual asymmetric emitter ports with visible internal ceramic alignment markers
Translucent side panels revealing layered capacitor architecture—a confidence display or warning
Charged-state indicator LED (faint blue) visible through the polymer when powered
Piezoelectric coupling rings emit faint iridescent interference patterns when discharge sequence is active
Absence of traditional sights—targeting is delegated to an integrated micro-laser (faint red dot, visible only in low light)
Serial plate located on the underside of the grip, deliberately obscured by hand position during normal operation
Minute exhaust ports along the slide for thermal dissipation, appearing as a row of pinpricks
The charging mechanism is a rotating collar rather than a traditional slide—unusual ergonomic choice
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small embossed 'BBc' logo (Bright Block Childcare) on the left side of the slide—understated and easily mistaken for generic branding. No visible serial number in standard viewing angles. A faint laser-etched designation 'PSVP-1 | 11/D' appears only under direct overhead light on the underside.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weapons in the field show minimal wear—the polymer resists traditional scarring, and most operators maintain meticulous cleanliness due to the weapon's sensitivity to contaminants near the emitter ports. Recovered units typically show cosmetic white stress marks on the grip from sustained tension, and occasional scorching around the emitter ports where backflash or skin residue has carbonized. Most examples carry visible evidence of field maintenance: thin lines of sealant around the capacitor access panel, occasional misaligned safety indicators from field repair, and sometimes improvised lens covers fashioned from medical tape.
